newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids mostly flat again, helped by crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids mostly flat again, helped by crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, helped by another rally in NYMEX crude, stayed little changed Friday in thin trade, but with falling demand on milder weather, few expected much upside near-term.

"The Merc will probably put a floor under resid for now, but the demand is not there and there is some supply coming in August," said one cash trader, noting cheaper East Coast city gate gas prices also were siphoning some demand.
But others said steady burns in Florida and expected high sulphur demand next month from Mexico should limit any downside.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased a dime Friday to $16.50-75 a barrel, while August one percent paper firmed slightly to $16.40-50 with stronger crude. September paper was still quoted near $16.25.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was marginally lower at $17.50-75 in the face of soft utility demand and decent supply.
High sulphurs in New York again were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still quoted at $15.25-50.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices remained stable, with one percent still in the high-$15s and three percent at $14.50-75.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate weekend gas prices slipped slightly Friday to about the $2.40/mmBtu level, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also fell about two cents to $2.22/mmBtu, or $13.99 a barrel.
